Simple Graphs

Graph TheoryLogicAlgorithms
Game: Place dots on the board and join them with lines to build a graph. Watch how many lines meet at each dot. There is nothing to win — explore what every graph must satisfy.
How to play: Click empty space to add a dot. Drag from one dot to another to add a line. Pop removes the last line; Reset clears the board.

Look for the math

A graph is a collection of dots (vertices) joined by lines (edges). Drawing one more line changes two numbers at once, and that is where the interesting facts come from.

Degrees

The degree of a vertex is the number of lines that touch it. Tick Show degrees to see the numbers beside the dots. Drawing the same line twice is allowed here, so each copy adds one to both degrees. A loop, when enabled, starts and ends at the same dot and adds two to its degree.

The handshaking fact

Every edge has two ends, so adding up all the degrees counts each edge exactly twice. Therefore total degree = 2 × number of edges, whatever the graph looks like.

Odd degrees come in pairs

Because the total degree is even, the sum of the odd degrees must also be even. That can only happen if there is an even number of odd-degree vertices: 0, 2, 4, and so on. Try to draw a graph with exactly one odd vertex — you will not be able to.

What was checked

The logic test builds random graphs with repeated edges and loops both enabled and disabled, and checks the handshaking equality and the even number of odd vertices on each. It also checks that a loop counts twice, that loops are refused when the option is off, and that Pop and Reset behave as the applet does.

Draw three dots and join them in a triangle. Every degree is 2; add a fourth line from one dot to another and see which two degrees become odd.
